title: DEFINITION
text:
A solitary pulmonary nodules (SPN) usually is defined as a focal opacity on chest radiograph or CT, which has following criteria:
1. It is relatively well defined.
2. It is surrounded, at least partially, by lung.
3. It is roughly spherical in shape.
4. It is 3 cm or less in diameter.

Homogenous soft tissue denity completely obscuring lung parenchyma behind.
Most common type of SPN.

Hazy opacity without obscuring underlying lung parenchyma.

title: CONTRAST ENHANCEMENT
text:
Recommended Protocol: 
Scan at 1 min intervals for 4 minutes following the start of injection.
A region of interest include about 60% of nodule diameter is use to measure enhancement.
NODULE ENHANCEMENT <  15 HU   - S/O  BENIGN LESION 
NODULE ENHANCEMENT 15-20 HU - S/O  INDETERMINATE LESION
NODULE ENHANCEMENT >  20  HU – S/O  MALIGNANT LESION 
SENSITIVITY  -  95  -100% 
SPECIFICITY  -70 -93 %
This applies only for nodules with the following selection criteria:
Nodule > 5mm
Relatively spherical
Homogeneous, no necrosis, fat or calcification
No motion or beam hardening artifacts
notes: contrast enhancement helps to differentiate benign vs malignant

title: 15 MIN DELAY
text:
Malignant nodules: 
 wash-in of  >25 HU 
 washout of 5-31 HU
 Benign nodules: 
  wash-in of < 25 H
  wash-in of >25 HU in combination with a washout of > 31 HU 
  wash-in of > 25 HU and persistent enhancement without washout
notes: after 15 min delay

title: GROWTH RATE ASSESSMENT
text:
Volume doubling time is the time required for a lesion to double its volume
VDT = t * log2
            log Vt/Vo
t= time difference
Vt= volume at time t
Vo= initial volume
1 VDT = 26% increase in the diameter of the nodule

title: Absence of growth over at least 2 yrs period : reliable Indicator of benignity, however exception is BAC.
COMPUTER AIDED DIAGNOSIS (AI)
text:
Integrated computer system that supports nodule identification, analysis of nodule size, morphology and textural analysis of internal structure of nodule by analysis of high resolution CT data.
The CAD system recognizes opacity lesions surrounded by lung parenchymal attenuation as nodules. Therefore, nodules in the subpleural, fissural and costophrenic angle areas might be missed. 
Not helpful to pick up lesions less than 4mm
Cannot replace the radiologist ; only supporting tool

title: ROLE OF DUAL ENERGY CT IN SPN
text:
DECT can decompose enhanced structures into soft tissue and iodine
Allows for differentiation of calcification from enhancing tissue by subtraction of iodine component
By single scanning after iodine injection, we can measure the degree of enhancement without an additional non enhanced CT

title: ROLE OF CONTRAST ENHANCED DYNAMIC MRI IN SPN
text:
Dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI is helpful in differentiating benign from malignant solitary pulmonary nodules
Absence of significant enhancement is a strong predictor that a lesion is benign.
Presence of  rim enhancement seen in –granuloma  and network or rim  enhancement seen in–hamartoma
Presence of homogeneous/heterogenous enhancement : malignancy

title: ROLE OF DW-MRI IN SPN
text:
SCALE ( study by Satoh et al ) are:
Nearly no signal intensity
Signal intensity between 1 and 3
Signal intensity almost equal to the spinal cord at thoracic spine
Higher signal than spinal cord
 SCORE OF 3 IS  THRESHOLD FOR DIFFERENTIATING BENIGN AND MALIGNANT NODULES

title: Disadvantages of MRI
text:
Poor resolution  
Cardiac and respiratory motion artifacts
Difficulty in detecting lesion  < 1 cm lesion
Not useful in peripheral  SPN due to signal loss

title: ROLE OF FDG-PET
text:
Malignant cells have upregulated metabolisms and proliferate rapidly.This results in marked uptake of FDG 
PET-CT plays an increasingly important role in the evaluation of solitary nodules.
PET has a very high sensitivity 95%, but a lesser specificity of only 81%
False negative  results  due to -   Carcinoids , BAC , Adeno with BAC component  , SPN < 10 mm
False positive results are due to –Active TB , Histoplasmosis ,   Rhematoid nodules ,Aspergillosis  , wegeners granulomatosis
Possibility of malignancy with negative FDG-PET is <5%
The SUV (Standarized uptake value) is more that 2.5 for lung cancers.

title: ROLE OF SPECT IN SPN
text:
The diagnostic ability of SPECT has been reported, with sensitivity (85 to 100%), specificity (90 to 100%) and accuracy of 85 to 100%.
Diagnostic accuracy for the pulmonary nodules over 2 cm in size between SPECT and FDG-PET is almost the same, However less sensitive than PET for nodules smaller than 2 cm

title: For Inderterminate SPN, method fo biopsy include:
Fleischner Guideline 2017
text:
These new guidelines should reduce the number of unnecessary follow-up examinations and provide clear management decisions.
Nodule characterization should be performed on thin-slice CT images ≤1.5 mm, since a small solid nodule may appear to have groundglass density on a thick slice due to partial-volume effect.

title: Risk Factors of Pulmonary Nodule Malignancy are
text:
History of heavy smoking
Exposure to asbestos.
Family history of lung cancer
Older age
Sex: Females > Males
Marginal spiculation
Upper lobe location
Multiplicity (< 5 nodules increases risk for malignancy)
Emphysema and pulmonary fibrosis.

title: ROUND ATELECTASIS
text:
FOLDED LUNG 
Chronic atelectasis that resembles mass 
X ray and ct – Peripherily located , wedge shaped opacity 
Based against focally thickened pleura, commonly at lung base
Crow feet  / comet tail of vessels sweeping into the margin of this opacity 
A rapidly forming pleural effusion produces an adjacent area of passive atelectasis 
A groove of visceral pleura may infold into the area of atelectasis and come to surround a part of it

notes: This is Conventional tomographic scan of the chest in a lateral projection shows a largemass by arrowhead in the right lower lobe of the lung. A curvilinear opacity mark by arrow, arises from the inferior pole of the mass and courses toward the hilum.
